An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty at 0.068 picoseconds.

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting an energy-dependent pattern that adheres to a power law with an index of 0.79 ± 0.19. We also discovered that the orientation of these anisotropy patterns supports their extragalactic origins, and that on a sky map, an equatorial-based dipolar component emerges when we consider the most energetic events separately. This finding can be understood in relation to the observed preference for low-energy maximum excitation values, often situated in the Frohlich zone, when the direction of the Sun is taken into account. These high-energy anisotropy measurements provide us with more constrained limits on theoretical models of very-high- and ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray propagation.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. Owing to its sophisticated design and reliability, the ATLAS detector successfully collected a comprehensive dataset during heavy ion and proton-proton runs. As a result, it facilitated precise measurements of the nuclear modification factor, obtained by dividing charged particle yields from heavy ion collisions by their proton-proton counterparts in various centrality ranges and rapidity intervals. Furthermore, this analysis reveals a notable variation in the nuclear modification factor with transverse momentum, showing a more pronounced trend in more peripheral collisions.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators, we can transform these commutation relations into algebraic equations, whose solvability is key to understanding whether a corresponding quantum Lie algebra exists. Using a method developed in prior research, we can determine the differential operators in detail, obtain an explicit representation and derive the associativity conditions for the resulting algebra. This approach is then applied to several examples, including the noncommutative harmonic oscillator, a model involving three-dimensional angular momentum and a generalized isotonic oscillator, to both verify prior findings and discover new results.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable and accurate image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 56 Gb/s in a real-world underwater environment. A piezoelectric actuator was used to introduce 2 µs-long, high-intensity optical bursts within the system. These bursts, resembling nonlinear effects commonly encountered in underwater communications, severely impacted the equality performance of a decision feedback equalizer (DFE). To investigate the dynamics of the bursts, researchers analyzed the average and variance of the equalized signals at the decision feedback equalizer input, as well as its phase, and mapped the average variance relationship. It was found that the average variance of the equalized signals accounts for nearly 90% of the variation in the DFE's equality performance, explaining the complex interaction between the bursts. Based on this finding, researchers developed a simple model to predict the impact of the bursts on the DFE's equality performance, considering the distribution and intensity of the optical bursts. Experimental validation confirmed the model's accuracy, outperforming previous methods by a significant margin (nearly 30 dB). Furthermore, to counteract the impact of the optical bursts on the DFE, researchers proposed adjusting the feedback coefficients of the DFE. Notably, these proposed approaches can be applied to other types of burst errors produced by decision cross-talk, providing better overall system performance.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate the dilation optimization process by casting it as a weight-pruning operation along the time axis. Our method learns dilation factors concurrently with weights during training and achieves notable gains in model compactness and inference efficiency without compromising accuracy. It produces a range of highly optimal TCN variants from a single starting model, surpassing the performance of custom-designed networks in both efficiency and accuracy.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study presents initial findings on the fluctuations of flow moments and cumulants in Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC, with an energy level of 5.02 TeV and an integrated luminosity of 0.04 nb, presented on 24th June 2016.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, our proposed method effectively employs ALBA's rules and algebraic language to reverse its computations in the DLE setting, thereby allowing the derivation of an inductive formula from its first-order correspondent.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be associated with a truth status: true, false, inconsistent, or undetermined. Furthermore, we investigate the efficiency of querying such data tables and the underlying computational costs of specific query types.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrating under mild conditions that maximum likelihood estimation yields reliable and normally-distributed estimates of model parameters. To evaluate the TV-PARX model's performance and forecasting capabilities in real-world scenarios, we conducted a series of Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we have applied the time-varying specification of the TV-PARX model to empirical data sets, analyzing new daily COVID-19 cases in Italy and corporate defaults in the US.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new objects from the same category. We
demonstrate NDFs in picking tasks, which involve positioning a handle at a
target location. By integrating NDFs into a reinforcement learning controller, we
achieve handle placement on unseen 3D coffee mugs. The NDF object representations
exhibit latent structural and semantic information, which can be utilized for
partial handle fit prediction and categorization of a object's orientation into
six-dimensional space.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D findings, production progress, and maintenance aspects during operation and maintenance phases.

We performed the first in-depth analysis of seven red giant members in the globular cluster Tonarzintla 2. This study is part of the CASILEN survey, which conducted a comprehensive observation of nine Galactocentric globular cluster groups. Utilizing the APOGEE-2 near-infrared spectrograph, we obtained high-resolution spectra for these stars and derived the cluster's age, metallicity, and velocity dispersion. The estimated age of Tonantzintla 2 is 8.7 to 10.1 billion years, with a metallicity of -0.53 to -0.61. The internal dynamics of the cluster are revealed by a velocity dispersion of 0.68 to 1.09 kilometers per second. The position of Tonantzintla 2 in the color-metallicity diagram is consistent with the average trajectory of the galactic bulge population, making it an ideal candidate for "spectral tomography" to study the formation of the bulge. This technique involves comparing the physical and chemical properties of blue and red sub-populations within a cluster to highlight the differences in the bulge's star formation history.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as well as initial findings, which reveal that the Isabelle Archive exhibits characteristics typical of scale-free networks, as evidenced by the distribution of node in-degrees in its dependency graph.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.569 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these earlier results have a larger systematic uncertainty.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, expansive, and minutely featured particles.  To study these intricate  
structures, we present a fully three-dimensional, computationally based  
method, integrating accurate geometric representations with robust simulation  
tools, enabling analysis of complex scenarios, including anular patches with  
micresonators, stacked elements, and offset patches.  

Through our method, we can evaluate and compare the outcomes of various  
designs, demonstrating, for instance, how element spacing influences localized  
resonance strength, and how different fabrication techniques yield different  
results.  Furthermore, our approach allows exploration of structural  
integrity, for instance, how the material and thickness of backplates influence  
metasurface durability.  

Additionally, we extend this method to investigate plasma interactions with  
complex metasurfaces, for instance, in future fusion reactors, where we  
evaluate the durability of surfaces subjected to prolonged plasma interactions.  

Overall, our computational framework provides an intricate tool for designing  
various metasurface applications, for instance, in antennas, filters,  
screening, and surface protection systems.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach using almost a decade's worth of data from the Keck telescope, which involved analyzing the effects of gravity on the background galaxies. Specifically, it presents the largest scale at which significant cosmic structures induce observable patterns in the distribution of these distant galaxies. Additionally, the arc exhibits unique characteristics in the magnification experienced by the background galaxies, which could provide valuable insights into the large-scale structures of the universe and potentially aid in answering fundamental questions about the cosmos.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined quickly, regardless of the system's absolute calibration. Our new approach employs high-speed, wide-field CCD photometry, typically used for time-variable astronomy, to examine the accuracy of this technique through analyses of the atmosphere and an experimental aerosol chamber. Our findings indicate that photometry based on stars can provide a reliable and precise method for measuring aerosol scattering profiles.

Recently, estimating a 6-Degree of Freedom (6DoF) object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has gained significant attention for its ability to rapidly provide pose predictions suitable for downstream applications like visualization, scene reconstruction, and augmented reality. A pose predictor's performance is heavily dependent on its hierarchical components, namely the feature hierarchy (backbone) and projection hierarchy. While the impact of innovative feature hierarchies on pose prediction performance is well-documented, the role of projection hierarchies has been largely disregarded. This study proposes a novel approach to enhance the Hough Projection Grouping (HPG) module, known as 2DHMap, to accommodate the multi-scale nature of predictions provided by the DeepHierarchicalNet (DeepHNet) feature hierarchy. Our proposed DeepHierarchicalHMap (DeepHHMap) architecture achieves superior pose estimation results on the YaleV2 dataset in comparison to its predecessor 2DHMap. Further enhancements to HPG are explored, leading to the integration of a correspondence learning module. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding state-of-the-art pose estimation results with Mean Average Reprojection Error (MARPE) of 5.48 on the YaleV2 dataset using the DeepHierarchicalNet (DeepHNet) feature hierarchy, and DeepHHMap (DeepHHNets) with a combined DeepHNet feature and projection hierarchy, achieving a remarkable MARPE of 4.91.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuities within materials without the need for complex mathematical expressions. Peridynamic models of dynamic fracture have revealed a transition to steady-state motion, where a distinct region around the tip of a crack forms and remains stable, despite initial research indicating that cracks always evolve by changing their surface area. This finding has profound implications, as it suggests that the existence of a stable, ring-like structure around the crack in solids may have a counterpart in certain astrophysical phenomena. Ring-shaped structures are commonly observed around black holes and neutron stars, and our research offers both theoretical and numerical proof of the formation of these structures during the progression of a crack. Additionally, we have explored the connection between peridynamics and other nonlocal mechanics models, as well as their experimental validation.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized, particularly in configurational sampling and phase material properties calculations. A new class of implicit Langevin algorithms was proposed recently, showcasing superior performance in computational efficiency when handling stiff interactions, including configurational entropy calculations. This research developed a general framework for solving the stochastic Poisson-Carathéodory equation, extending the traditional master equation solution, and discovered that these algorithms satisfy the Itô interpretation, ensuring the independence of stochastic increments from the increment's magnitude. This discovery paves the way for incorporating large jumps in additive noise, such as the Monte-Carlo method, into simulations. By analyzing the drift modification due to the diffusion term, we introduced a modified solver for the drift component, facilitating the adaptation of these algorithms to various noise models. Two examples were examined, including a test problem and simulations of the Lennard-Jones system, demonstrating that these algorithms with implicit treatment of the drift term outperformed their counterparts in both computational efficiency and accuracy of the mean energy calculation.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations start only after the event, when the individual black holes have already come together. To better understand the full picture, researchers need data on how the system behaves before the merger event. In this study, we investigate the merger of two binary black holes in an environment with low-mass stars and wave dark matter. Our findings show that the gravitational waves produced can both excite the wave dark matter into more intense peaks, as well as strip it away from the system by being absorbed by the merging black holes. In contrast, the low-mass stars are either torn apart and funneled into the system by being absorbed. These processes have significant implications for the amount of matter that might be emitted during the merger, as well as the merger rate of binary black holes in systems with stars and wave dark matter.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement influenced by both elasticity and friction. A detailed analysis in a Hilbert space reveals how the spectrum's asymptotic distribution and structure evolve. It demonstrates that specific eigenvector characteristics form a complete and orthonormal basis. Consequently, we derive the exponential stability of the associated semigroup directly. Notably, we show that under these connectivity conditions, stability is guaranteed even in the absence of elasticity along the edges.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution but discovered these lenses introduced image distortion. This problem was investigated and a new lens material called Stycast 1090SI was proposed as an alternative. The acoustic properties of this novel material were examined alongside PMMA to determine its feasibility. Computational simulations and practical tests using two different materials, PMMA and Stycast 1090SI, showed both materials significantly enhance the detection capabilities of sensitive devices. Notably, the Stycast lens exhibited lower levels of distortion compared to the PMMA lens, which could have implications for photoacoustic tomography technology.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, the connectivity between nodes can differ by layer and the significance of nodes can vary across layers. These factors influence the central position of nodes in each layer and overall central tendency in the multi-layered network. Our approach takes these factors into account when calculating eigenvector centrality through the element-wise product of multi-layer adjacency matrices and a diagonal multi-layer importance matrix, and we further examine how differences in connectivity and node importance across layers affect the results.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an interpretable way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into raw images through a realistic process, mimicking real-world camera functions. By incorporating our proposed module and comparing it to a baseline of separate demosaicking and deblurring steps, we demonstrate improved results, particularly for intermediate motion artifacts caused by motion blur. Alternatively, this model can be applied to mosaic images with motion blur by replacing the demosaicking component with a suitable network, yielding comparable performance to handling raw images directly.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.
This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as water seal formation and breakdown, which is vital for understanding the forces involved. A time seal curve is defined to characterize this water-filling process, and the conditions for the seal to form and break are mapped out in a diagram. The seal formation and breaking conditions are analyzed in relation to the forces of gravity, drag, and pressure, and the results indicate that the one-dimensional force balance best explains the sealing processes for a broad range of conditions. Furthermore, the study finds that an analytical theory of pressure best explains the seal behavior for both slow and fast movement regimes, and that the seal curve formation and breaking points diverge less when influenced by surface tension than when in a state of negligible wettabilty.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially conserved. Our main findings are as follows: nearly all calculable Type IIB $\mathcal{N}=2$ EFTs break their R-symmetry to a nonuniversal level. Moreover, if a theory has residual R-symmetry, it will necessarily break its duality group to a nonuniversal level. We also examined bulk and membrane charges in relation to Witten's generalized $\theta$-terms. Our analysis indicates that the conservation of any membraic charge implies a violation of any bulk charge, regardless of whether it is matter-like or R-symmetry. As an illustration, adding an Euler charactereistic flux can result in Ischerman-Kahraman type anomalies between Hodge numbers in the limit of highly compactified M-theory.

Mobile devices frequently host multiple simultaneous applications that often require access to sensitive personal data. To prevent malicious apps from exfiltrating this data, mobile operating systems typically isolate apps into distinct security domains. However, these systems are vulnerable to attacks that exploit cross-domain attacks. Transcendental extraction attacks, for instance, utilize physically-isolated hardware to secure sensitive data. This type of hardware, however, is often underutilized on commercial mobile devices, where hardware security modules and trusted execution environments are also used for security-critical functions. In response to this limitation, we introduce a novel security concept called TUE (Transcendental-Only-Used Exclusively) hardware, which defines hardware that is designed and reserved for preventing and countering attack scenarios. We then present TuWHAM (Transcendental-Only-Used Hardware Allocation Method), a security framework that ensures transcendentality by allocating hardware that is intended for countering attack scenarios to security-critical applications. TuWHAM achieves this by first distinguishing between attack scenarios and defense mechanisms, and then ensuring that attack scenarios are contained within distinct security domains, and finally, assigning TUE hardware to these domains.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to no more than an $\epsilon$ fraction of all training episodes. Notably, this attack model surpasses previously considered methods. We established a key finding that no reinforcement learning algorithm can discover an optimal policy better than $O(\epsilon)$ under these circumstances. Interestingly, we discovered that the natural policy gradient method can be robust when the corruption is bounded and is capable of finding an $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$-optimal policy. We developed a Filtered Policy Gradient (FPG) algorithm, capable of tolerating unbounded reward corruption, and achieved an $O(\epsilon^{1/4})$-optimal policy. The FPG algorithm represents a pioneering solution to robust reinforcement learning in scenarios with significant adversarial interference. Moreover, we verified the effectiveness of an FPG implementation utilizing a neural network on MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as quantum electrodynamics with extreme Rabi splitting, is being intensely studied. This area of study uses closely related photons that interact with one another indirectly, enabling researchers to explore complex phenomena outside of singular effects. Nevertheless, external factors such as an external magnetic field are required to eliminate the energy difference between dark and bright excitons in the quantum systems, which hinders comparisons with bright excitons in terms of oscillation frequencies and amplitudes. This study is the first to observe Rabi splitting in terms of dark excitons and is also the first to do so, without relying on an external magnetic field. As a result, this study demonstrates that dark states can be activated and controlled, which could open the way to using these states for quantum applications.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of glide symmetries in perpendicular directions using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. This model contains horizontal and vertical hopping terms and reveals two distinct non-equivalent Dirac cones within the first Brillouin zone along a high-symmetry path. These cones can be modified through various perturbations of the Hamiltonian. These perturbations disrupt the lattice symmetries by applying differing onsite potentials at the lattice sites, which causes the Dirac cones to collapse into semi-Dirac cones and nodal lines, or even cross each other. Next, we applied a magnetic field to this lattice, resulting in the cones being filled with Landau levels and leaving remnants of the semi-Dirac cones and nodal lines, whereas the Dirac cones transform into the famous triply-degenerate zeroth Landau level.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess abundant non-classical behavior, thereby conferring a quantum advantage for executing various computational and communication tasks more efficiently than states enriched with only one extra photon.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a custom descriptor for chemically repetitive polymers and integrates it with the framework. We evaluate the enhanced method's performance with two integer programming models, assessing their ability to maximize or maintain polymer properties while minimizing chemical descriptor values. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively predicts polymer characteristics and outperforms existing polymer modeling approaches in multiple property tests, including density and refractive index.

This paper presents a unified approach to addressing certain complex optimization challenges. Problems of control, estimation, and system design can be redefined as optimization problems subject to specific constraints. However, given the infinite dimensionality of these issues, it becomes necessary to employ numerical techniques to approximate a solution. We explore specific methods used in simultaneous direct approaches, specifically the transcription process. Our focus is on collocation and time integration methods, using a dual-patient ventilation scenario during the COVID-19 pandemic as an illustrative case study. We first model ventilation as a partial differential equation, and then transform the problem of optimizing airflow into a set of discrete optimization tasks.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shapes and sizes of tumors, and in some cases, partial segmentation. A new model called esDDAUnet was created to automatically and accurately segment tumors in CT scans of the esophagus by combining an improved attention-unet structure with dense attention modules and asymptotic cross-scale connection. The esDDAUnet was then compared to the original UNet and U-Net++ while tested on a publicly available dataset, and outperformed the others in terms of precision, recall, and Dice similarity coefficient.

The expense and environmental impact of drilling oil and gas wells necessitates
geosteering, a process of adjusting a well's trajectory in real-time to stay
within oil and gas payzones. Traditional approaches to geosteering rely on
estimating key formations using well log interpretation, which can be
challenging due to the complexity of modern wells and potential noise in logs.
Furthermore, conventional methods often use a deterministic framework that
underestimates uncertainties in formation estimates, a critical aspect in
determining payzone boundaries. To address these challenges, we designed an
algorithm to efficiently interpret a range of well logs, adjusting for various
effects to isolate the signature of specific formations. Building on this, we
developed a method to quantify uncertainties in formation estimates by
constructing ensemble-based lookup tables. A case study using a synthetic well
demonstrated that our approach is robust to well log transformations and
preserves uncertainties, allowing us to manage the complexity of modern wells.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on recognizing entities within other entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which do not adequately account for the hierarchical nature of nested entities. This work overcomes this limitation by modeling nested entities as a holistic structure and proposing a new parser to parse this structure. Notably, our proposed method is a nested dependency parser, which builds upon successful parsing models by adapting them to nested data. Evaluations on three NER datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, achieving state-of-the-art results with the holistic structure modeling and holistic parsing approach.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as enumerating objects in higher-dimensional spaces using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference. We look at curves defined by equations that are smooth, or at least have many smooth points, and count the number of curves that are tangent at specified points at four specific points. We express both the number of such curves that can be parameterized by specific points, as well as the number of such curves that can be considered in a "signed" way using values from specific algebraic structures, in terms of the values of a new, modified version of the equations when converted to a simplified form. We demonstrate the applicability of this approach by examining the number of such curves that are considered with values from specific algebraic structures, such as points from specific algebraic structures, as well as their "smoothness" or "semi-stability".

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract interference between different technologies operating in the same frequency range, we design and execute a new method for calculating the distance between nodes. The aim of this approach is to minimize the average error in location estimation, and when compared to ideal, interference-free results, we have achieved a level of accuracy of less than half a metre using actual hardware.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi in written form.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing human selection criteria and description quantity to effectively assess automatic image description systems.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are highly effective in blocking X-rays and exhibit low signals when used as x-ray imaging sources, making them valuable in both traditional and digital radiography. One of the variants of this material, the $\gamma$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ phase, displays promising properties for improving the images in x-ray imaging, resulting from its crystal's ability to change shape under x-ray radiation. To better understand this phase's potential, we conducted simulations to determine the electronic, mechanical, and optical properties of Ta$_2$O$_5$-$\gamma$ in detail. We also developed methods to discover the crystal's different forms and found that our results can be applied to optimize the design of radiography filters made from this material. Furthermore, we discovered significant potential in using these filters doped with other rare earth metals, such as neodymium, to enhance the images produced by this material.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but ignored a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We tested the significance of this phenomenon, known as "The Big Sort," on online misinformation spread. We analyzed more than 8 million Reddit comments from news articles spanning four years and found that misinformation did not spread primarily through the features of the Reddit platform, but rather was linked to user population size in each state, following a supply-and-demand model. Furthermore, variations in misinformation dissemination were explained by local personality traits and cultural characteristics rather than economic, social, or political conditions. In areas where residents are less diligent in nature, and cultures place little emphasis on adherence to norms, we found increased circulation of false information.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection algorithm called HALFADO, designed to identify suspicious entities that manipulate traffic measurements in dynamic systems. HALFADO operates under a robust statistical framework, allowing it to function effectively even as system conditions change continuously. The algorithm's performance is improved through the innovative HALFADO+ variant, which incorporates a fast, localized detection method underpinning HALFDO. A comprehensive experimental evaluation, conducted using diverse data sets including real-world DDoS attacks and controlled experiments with the BELLA framework, demonstrates HALFADO's capability to accurately identify malicious entities with high precision and low latency. Furthermore, HALFADO's efficient use of resources allows for practical implementation in real-time scenarios.

Humans employ spoken language to teach other people, along with other methods such as verbal guidance, by example, and by observation. Employing spoken language to teach a robot specific tasks is a significant topic of research in robotics and requires further investigation to enhance a robot's ability to learn tasks efficiently. A key aspect of this research is analyzing how human instructors verbally describe tasks they are performing. To address this, we created a dataset that captures both audio and video of a human teaching a robot to operate a coffee machine, by demonstrating the task multiple times and collecting additional information, effectively giving a key to replicating the task. We examined this dataset to understand how human instructors articulate their instructions, focusing on speech speed, pronunciation, and the use of filler words.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore the application of this algorithm to analyze the behavior of λ-terms resulting from parallel rewriting under beta-reduction, by utilizing an existing model that predicts the outcomes of beta-convergence and supercomputationality.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models. A promising approach to address this issue is through the study of conformal field theory, specifically $c$-number worldline paths, as initially proposed by Hathorn and Sotiriadis. A key, yet unresolved, question in this context is the identification of the initial and final states that define the evolution of the state's complexity. A potential solution to this issue is to consider the boundary conditions where the velocities of the paths correspond to the Fefferman-Vassilevich expansion coefficients, representing the coefficients of the vector fields that generate the evolution from a free theory to the interacting one. An overarching method for obtaining these velocities is to utilize the Euler-Arnold equation, a nonlinear variant of the Schrodinger equation. In this work, the Euler-Arnold equations are applied to a one-dimensional interacting model and the large-$c$ limit of its central charge. A direct correlation between field theory complexity and the sum of the Euler-Arnold equation's mid-point solution modes is found, especially in the $c \to \infty$ limit of the central charge.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights key characteristics that such a framework should possess. Furthermore, this paper highlights key research directions for advancing research in this domain.

Using a sophisticated mathematical model known as the Fisher information matrix, we determined the minimum mass required for a hypothetical Planet X to have a measurable gravitational impact on the current known planets. This analysis was based on data from the JPL Developmental ephemeris (DE440) model. We found that for a Planet X located in the outer Neptune's resonance, it would need to be at least 0.5 Earth masses to have a detectable effect. For a Planet X in the outer Solar System beyond the Neptune's resonance, the requirement is that it would need to be 2 Earth masses or more. These thresholds apply to detection in the outer Solar System specifically, not in the inner regions near Venus and Earth's orbits. For any object with these specifications, it is highly probable that it would have been identified in the wide-field surveys like Pan-STARRS1 and the Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey. We also explored various alternative models for a Planet X, but these models would need to be more precise in the future.

Translation memory has long been recognized as effective in enhancing both
statistical and neural machine translation systems. Notably, when supplied with
a large amount of parallel data, translation memory proves particularly useful
for improving translation quality. In contrast, this study explores whether
a monolingual dataset can be leveraged to supplement existing machine translation
models, compensating for any lack of parallel data. We present an approach that
integrates supply-driven and demand-driven access to monolingual data within a
neural translation framework. Our experiments indicate that this proposed
approach is capable of mitigating any shortfalls in parallel data, regardless of
whether it is compared against a system utilizing only demand-driven TM access or a
system with ample parallel data. The results are further showcased through
state-of-the-art translations for both low-resource and high-resource language
pairs. The code is made available on GitHub for reference: https://github.com/
zhangxv/TM-Augmentation-NMT.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. These patterns are predicted to originate from previous black hole mergers and evaporation events. We analyzed the Planck and WMAP data using a machine learning tool called HawkingNet, and initially found potential anomalies resembling low-variance circles and Hawking points. However, these anomalies were later removed, and upon re-examination, we found no statistically significant evidence supporting the existence of low-variance circles or Hawking points in the CMB sky. Additionally, we found that characteristics similar to primary CMB anisotropies are rare in simulated SNR maps of Hawking points, but found as dark matter subhalos in the present universe.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research proposes a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in superior performance on various datasets and settings when paired with existing models.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommendation systems. Single cross-domain models are often limited by the lack of support for data sparsity in both related and target domains. To tackle this challenge, we propose a innovative concept of multi-sparse-domain recommendation, which considers recommendation systems that related, target domains exhibit sparse data while remaining unrelated to each other. Adopting the innovative concept, we present a novel framework called ECHiCRL, which tackles the multi-sparse-domain challenge through an alternative perspective of users expressing aspect preferences across diverse product dimensions. To facilitate the learning process of users' aspect preferences in a comprehensive manner, we employ a multi-task framework that simultaneously leverages multi-sparse data through embedding prediction and self-supervised contrastive learning tasks. Specifically, related domain related-embeddings and target-domain target-embeddings are predicted, while related-embeddings' negative sampling and cross-domain consistency loss are utilized for the purpose of enhancing the consistency of representations across different domains. Experimental validation on Amazon datasets demonstrates that ECHiCRL outperforms state-of-the-art competitors in terms of accuracy.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications. Examples of these applications, such as reducing semidefinite matrices to positive semidefinite matrices, can be found within this package.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis. Several approaches have been explored to develop scalable and dependable master slave workflows for radiology, but handling the multi-class output pattern has proved challenging due to data sparsity. A novel, unsupervised method is proposed to learn hidden quality controls from sparse relevant cases and generalize to a broader population, employing a generative model with a shared latent space. In an experimental evaluation, it is demonstrated that this approach yields higher quality results compared to alternative strategies, particularly in populations with a diverse range of image quality.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

Intel Optane DC Persistent Memory modules present an intriguing option for designers of memory-intensive applications, allowing data to persist beyond a system's shutdown. By treating Optane DC as an extension of main RAM, developers can access data stored on it like they would in regular memory. However, the performance implications of this feature are still largely unexplored. Our research fills this knowledge gap, providing a comprehensive analysis of Intel Optane DC persistent memory system efficiency on Intel Xeon E5-4650 processor-based platforms. Our findings reveal that data transfer speeds using Optane DC match those of EXT4 file systems, but fall short of non-volatile RAM. We also explore the system's sensitivity to block sizes and mount options, as well as the impact of different data organization methods like RAID and mirroring.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results confirm that both GdSn3 and CmSn3 are full Kondo systems with distinct magnetic behaviors; GdSn3 exhibits an antiferromagnetic order, whereas CmSn3 displays a paramagnetic state. GdSn3 and CmSn3 also exhibit Sn-based topological Dirac materials with large energy gaps when the Gd/Cm sites are considered. The GdxCm1-xSn3 compounds ($x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75$) display varying degrees of Gd3+ and Cm3+ mixed valency, resulting in an energy gap closure as the composition shifts from the extremes to the middle.

The standard model of particle physics has been successfully tested for nearly a century, yet there are still several unanswered questions. One potential solution lies in the discovery of exotic hadrons beyond the conventional hybrid and multi-hadron states. The SHADe experiment at SPALAN in the future could play a key role in identifying these exotic hadrons by focusing on the production of charm quarks in p-p collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 2 GeV. The experiment will analyze the production of charmed quarks, the subsequent formation of $D^0$ and $D^+$ mesons and potentially search for additional baryons and mesons containing these mesons. Precise detectors and advanced particle identification systems will be utilized to collect a vast amount of data, allowing researchers to measure cross-sections of hadrons and spacial and temporal distributions of particles. The formation of hadrons will be investigated through the measurement of flow coefficients and elliptic flow, as well as through the analysis of thermal parameters and velocities of hadrons. The formation of a quark-gluon plasma and hadron gas will also be explored, as well as the possibility of forming hadrons within a polytrope equation of state.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Stong established a connection between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. This paper extends S. Shintani's work on the B-type finite Coxeter groups, proving that any element within the symmetric group Sn+1 can be uniquely expressed as a product of various powers of the standard Coxeter generators.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio $\Gamma$ and the radial distribution of matter density within halos $\rho(r)$. Based on this analysis, we demonstrated that incorporating weak lensing information can reduce Hubble diagram scatter from its current 0.11 level to 0.09, and we established relationships between weak lensing convergence and both the traditional external affinity principle as well as the Baade-Wesselman rule.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes and further relevant references are included. 

The concluding chapter covers the pathwise approach.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, although a lack of understanding regarding their formation mechanisms has hindered progress. We demonstrate precise control over the concentration and distribution of T centers in silicon light-speed material using laser damage, allowing for detailed investigation of their magnetic properties. By combining this with high-resolution spectroscopy, we find that T centers can be modeled as a pair of closely spaced defect centers in the silicon. We also report the first measurement of their hyperfine splitting, which varies from 127 to 155 microelectronvolts. Furthermore, we reveal an unusual phenomenon known as an avoided crossing in their energy levels, indicating complex electronic behavior. Our findings set the stage for detailed theoretical investigation and provide a foundation for developing reliable quantum information technologies based on T centers.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by comparing conventional image processing methods, such as morphological analysis and regional growth algorithms, in order to explore their application and effectiveness.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions and symbolic evaluation functions, allowing us to derive $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$. Our findings demonstrate intriguing connections with circulant matrices and Galois fields, while showcasing the potential for $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ to be applied in computationally efficient contexts.

The high activity levels on solar-type stars can significantly pollute the velocity measurements obtained from the lines in their spectra. This effect becomes particularly pronounced in active phases and cannot be disregarded in the assessment of potential Habitable Zones located around these stars. In this research, we investigated how to mitigate this effect by modifying the line lists employed in least-squares deconvolution analysis. We conducted a study on six K-dwarf and subgiant stars, spanning the range from 0.66 to 0.99 solar masses and activity levels from moderately inactive to very active. In order to analyse the impact of line lists on the residual spectra and their effect on radial velocity dispersion, we examined two approaches: using (i) lines with varying natural widths or (ii) lines that are either abundant or scarce. Our analysis revealed that in cases of low activity levels, both strategies yielded similar results, whereas in very active stars, they produced significantly different outcomes. In contrast to traditional methods that utilise broad lines to mitigate the effect of scattered noise among the narrow lines, our analysis indicated that in very active stars, selecting the most abundant narrow lines would produce the best results. This approach minimises the effect of the mismatch in line shapes caused by the extensive broadening of the spectral lines dominated by stellar activity. As a consequence, this research demonstrates that there exists an optimal line list that can achieve the maximum mitigation of stellar activity for each individual star, which is directly related to its mass and activity

This research paper proposes a pair of methods to enhance the efficiency of a wireless sensor network, specifically in reducing the duration and consumption of a network survey. Initially, we introduce 'H-RSSLE', a quality assessment technique for sensor connections, accounting for various factors including link speed, data reliability, and consumption. Subsequently, we present 'H-RSSLE' as a hierarchical method of organizing and collecting data using a set of clusters and sectors, leveraging the efficiency of a few high-quality sensors.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into 3 groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the input, another that uses partial
context by isolating part of the feature map, and one that uses full context
without isolation.
Our evaluation method assesses the effect of context for each deep detector
category systematically. A specially designed dataset is created to test the
effect of context for the first category. Moreover, we evaluate all three
detector categories with the newly created dataset as well as PASCAL VOC.
Our experiments show that providing context information to the deep detector
significantly improves performance.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations, which involves two key variables, $u$ and $v$. The given system exhibits a nonhomogeneous structure, a singular Turdinger-Moser growth, and a Kirchhoff coefficient that may take on zero values. By applying a critical Sobolev embedding, variational techniques, and critical point theory, we are able to establish both infinite and isolated solution existence results for the system, thereby addressing some of the limitations of previous research.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property (SCP) or the strong Rayleigh property (SRP). Our findings concerning SCP measures yield new subgaussian bounds for sufficiently Lipschitzian functions of such vectors, improving upon previous multiplicative factors. For SRP, we derive subgaussian sub- bounds for two types of sufficiently Lipschitzian functions, specifically, a monotone increasing function and a function with a monotone gradient, of this kind of random vector.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This study explores the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. Specifically, we investigate the cause of the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in hadron production, accounting for the connection between the helicity distribution $g_1$ and the twist-3 dihadron fragmentation function. Using a spectator model, we calculate the interference term between $s$-wave and $p$-wave and estimate this asymmetry at various experiments, including COMPASS, JLab 12 GeV, and the future EIC. Our analysis suggests that the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in SIDIS can serve as a key test for the dihadron fragmentation function.

We've established a connection between Fock's 1930s coordinate transformation, a key transformation in the conformal structure of Minkowski space, and the de Sitter space. This link enables us to derive de Sitter's invariant form from Fock's equation and recover the de Sitter space's intrinsic properties. This procedure further reveals that Fock's coordinate transformation is equivalent to the global de Sitter space parameterization, and we've obtained the Patch de Sitter space parameterization from a linear de Sitter space coordinate transformation.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished by a combination of invariant data, consisting of characteristic polynomials of matrix subsets and specific integer relationships.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with a lightweight ranking method, this framework effectively suggests related entities to users on Wikipedia. We evaluate our approach through both offline and real-world online tests, demonstrating that our embeddings and recommendations exhibit desirable quality and user engagement. Furthermore, this framework can be adapted to other entity recommendation systems by leveraging entity-interpretable information from knowledge graphs.

A key obstacle in kidney transplantation is the high rate of available kidneys that go unused due to incompatibility with potential recipients. Blood type and a variety of antibodies influence kidney compatibility, and the number of people with a blood type other than O is significantly higher than those with blood type O. The process of kidney compatibility checking can be modeled using a graph, and researchers have long sought to find optimal ways to perform surgeries based on connected subgraphs. In this study, we focus on a specific graph, composed of multiple disjoint cycles and a collection of odd cycles, and aim to perform a surgery on the graph by matching a fixed number of edges. When the collection of odd cycles consists of a single cycle of a certain length, we have a solution that minimizes the number of triangles in the surgery for any given graph and cycle length. Additionally, if the collection of odd cycles consists of a single cycle of a certain length, we have a solution that minimizes the number of triangles in the surgery for any graph and cycle length. These results have a direct application in kidney compatibility checking, where we find the optimal way to perform a surgery based on a specific graph, and this can be done in a polynomial amount of time.

Implicit copulas are the primary choice for analyzing dependencies in complex scenarios due to their ability to effectively model dependence in high-dimensional spaces. The text presents a comprehensive overview of this broad category, encompassing copulas such as elliptical, skew t, factor, time series, and regression copulas, highlighting their key characteristics and applications. The discussion explains how the auxiliary representation of implicit copulas facilitates scalability and usability in statistical modeling, addressing concerns like parameter estimation, likelihood calculation, and model parsimony. The text also covers Bayesian estimation techniques for implicit copulas and the benefits of employing these models in conjunction with time series and regression models, which are the subject of current research advancements. The advantages of using implicit copulas are further illustrated through the examination of econometric applications, including analyses of macroeconomic time series and financial asset pricing.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical analysis of the word vectors used to represent terms from the Loughran-McDonald's Polarities dataset, effectively examining the hidden meanings of these vectors. By focusing on the coherence and comparability of these embeddings, we aim to assess the inherent "semantics" of the word vectors. Notably, our examination reveals a stark discrepancy between the high coherence of the embeddings and their low comparability, suggesting that while the embeddings excel at identifying similar words, they fall short in accurately reflecting the true polarity of terms when compared to the established Lemmata labels. However, a notable improvement in this performance is observed when utilizing the BERT representation of the terms.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

Current versions of the Lambek Calculus used in computational linguistics are expanded upon a classical basis using unary modal operators. This work explores the application of a quantum interpretation of these calculi, specifically by utilizing the Quotational Calculus of Linear Subspaces to replace the modal calculation. Replacing each extended Lambek Calculus component with its QSLL counterpart results in a new system, Lambeli-Quot, that maintains the same proof-theoretic complexity as its modal predecessor, while offering a more efficient linear representation. As an alternative, non-modal approach, Lambeli-Quot provides an equally powerful framework for natural language syntax analysis, while also enabling the development of more efficient parsing algorithms. This study presents initial non-modal interpretations for the calculi strong, modular, and uniform embedding, as well as a corresponding efficient parsing algorithm.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding equilibria, learning rationalizable behavior that steers clear of dominated strategies is a fundamental objective. However, existing algorithms in the general multiplayer games scenario are limited to specific games in the two-player context and lack the ability to converge to rationalizable equilibria efficiently. We present a novel algorithm capable of learning $O(\log(1/\epsilon))$-approximate rationalizable strategies in the multiplayer, epsilon accurate scenario. Our algorithm's performance can be significantly enhanced when agents' payoff functions exhibit Lipschitz continuity, allowing it to achieve an $\Omega(\log(1/\epsilon))$-approximation for bandwidth-limited protocols in the two-player context. Moreover, our algorithm's communication requirements are on par with the best-known approaches in this setting.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs of key properties of the model, particularly its early stages and the phase where the epidemic spreads rapidly. They also found that under certain conditions, there are sharp thresholds where the model suddenly switches between two completely different behaviours. It has been proven that these transitions are more dramatic if the model is changed to only form new connections to uninfected nodes, where the model suddenly switches from no infections to complete spread.

In this study, we examine Cotton solitons within the context of almost Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds. Initially, we establish the incompatibility of such solitons when the potential vector field is directly aligned with the Reeb vector field. Then, assuming the potential vector field is perpendicular to the Reeb vector field, we demonstrate that on non-Kenmotsu almost Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds with the Reeb vector field being an eigen vector of the Ricci operator, a steady Cotton soliton emerges, characterizing a manifold that is locally identical in geometry to the warped product space $\mathbb{H}^2(-4) \times \mathbb{R}$.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurately fitting probability density functions. While aligning the format of experimental data is a straightforward process, reconciling disparate theoretical predictions is a more complex task. Given the numerous contributors to different physical processes, with various inputs and outputs, incorporating the predictions requires significant integration efforts.
